name: dead_air_then_burst
doc: A long stretch of dead air (the speaker is quiet / off-mic) followed by a burst of well-separated claims. Tests that (a) the trailing-silence window flush fires cleanly on the last pre-silence thought, (b) the rolling buffer does not carry stale words across the dead-air gap into the burst (no cross-gap window contamination), and (c) every claim in the burst is recovered once speech resumes. Should-pass-clean: the pre-silence claim airs, the gap produces nothing, and all burst claims air. The gap is >WINDOW_TRAIL_SILENCE_MS so the last thought flushes; the burst claims are spaced >3.6s so they never fuse.

finals.text: Quick one before we go quiet. Octopuses have three hearts.
Honey never spoils, they found edible honey in ancient tombs.
Goldfish have a three second memory.
And the Great Wall of China is visible from space with the naked eye.

expected.note: last thought before dead air → trailing-silence flush → airs

expected.utterance: Honey never spoils, they found edible honey in ancient tombs.
expected.note: first claim of the burst, after the gap → airs

expected_scorecard.status_note: should-pass-clean: pre-silence claim + all 3 burst claims recover, verify and air (4 aired); the resume filler ('Okay we are back') produces a no-claim check and airs nothing; dead air produces no phantom cards (checked==4, exactly the real claims). (claim_recall_pct/gate_correctness_pct unbounded: the generic filler 'Okay we are back' falls below the scorecard's fuzzy-match threshold so it scores as 'missed' rather than 'no-claim' — a matcher artifact; the pipeline emitted the no-claim check, asserted via no-claim>=1.)
